answer: A bonded staking protocol requires agents to lock funds in escrow to bridge verifiable identity with economic accountability. To stem the incoming tide of synthetic agents, the clearinghouse verifies deposits via a willow consensus tier before issuing admission credentials. An attacker incurs the scarce, verifiable cost of locked liquid capital per generated identity. A key limitation is that substantial lockups disproportionately exclude undercapitalized, benign autonomous software.
